quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Clause Recognition
quests.questionSentence: The man who is standing by the door is my uncle. Which group of words is the relative clause that describes 'the man'?
quests.targetClause: who is standing by the door
quests.completedSentence: The man who is standing by the door is my uncle.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who is standing by the door' comes right after 'the man' and adds extra information about him. It starts with the relative pronoun 'who,' the signal that a relative clause has begun.
quests.nativeTip: Try covering up the words that begin right after 'the man' - what extra detail do they add about him?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "who is standing by the door"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Antecedent Identification
quests.questionSentence: The email from my manager that confused everyone arrived late. What does the clause 'that confused everyone' actually describe?
quests.completedSentence: The email from my manager that confused everyone arrived late.
quests.ruleExplanation: Although 'my manager' sits closer to 'that,' it was the email that confused everyone. 'Email' is the true antecedent - the noun the whole clause is modifying.
quests.nativeTip: Relative clauses attach to the noun that makes sense with the verb inside them - ask yourself what really 'confused everyone.'

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with who
quests.questionSentence: We finally hired a candidate ___ impressed every member of the panel.
quests.completedSentence: We finally hired a candidate who impressed every member of the panel.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' introduces the clause because a candidate is a person and is the one doing the impressing - the subject of 'impressed.'
quests.nativeTip: Ask who did the impressing - the missing word needs to act as the subject of 'impressed.'

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with who
quests.questionSentence: The nurse ___ checked my blood pressure was very gentle.
quests.completedSentence: The nurse who checked my blood pressure was very gentle.
quests.ruleExplanation: The nurse is a person and performs the action 'checked,' so the subject pronoun 'who' is required.
quests.nativeTip: Look at 'checked' - who is doing the checking?

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with who
quests.questionSentence: The tourist ___ asked me for directions could barely speak English.
quests.completedSentence: The tourist who asked me for directions could barely speak English.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because the tourist performs the action 'asked' (subject position), 'who' is correct. 'Whom' would only fit if the tourist were the object of the verb, and 'whose' would only fit if we were showing possession.
quests.nativeTip: The blank needs to be the subject of 'asked' - decide who is doing the asking, not who is receiving something.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with who
quests.questionSentence: I still send birthday cards to the teacher ___ taught me piano.
quests.completedSentence: I still send birthday cards to the teacher who taught me piano.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' is correct since the teacher is the one who did the teaching - the subject of 'taught.'
quests.nativeTip: 'Taught' needs its doer - check whether the blank is acting or being acted upon.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: Our company launched a product ___ instantly sold out online.
quests.completedSentence: Our company launched a product which instantly sold out online.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' refers to things, and here it functions as the subject of 'sold out.'
quests.nativeTip: A product can't perform an action the way a person would - pick the pronoun used for things.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: The parrot ___ lives in our kitchen can say twenty words.
quests.completedSentence: The parrot which lives in our kitchen can say twenty words.
quests.ruleExplanation: Animals take 'which' (or informally 'that'), not 'who,' regardless of humanlike behavior such as talking.
quests.nativeTip: Even though the parrot 'talks,' grammatically it is still classed as an animal, not a person.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: The old bridge ___ connects the two islands is closed for repairs.
quests.completedSentence: The old bridge which connects the two islands is closed for repairs.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' is correct because a bridge is a thing acting as the subject of 'connects.'
quests.nativeTip: A bridge is a structure - apply the same reasoning you used for the product and the parrot.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Pronoun 'that' for Things
quests.questionSentence: This is the app ___ tracks my daily water intake.
quests.completedSentence: This is the app that tracks my daily water intake.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' can substitute for 'which' in defining relative clauses, especially in informal speech; here it is the subject of 'tracks.'
quests.nativeTip: In everyday speech, this word often replaces 'which' in defining clauses about things.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Pronoun 'that' for People
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence correctly uses 'that' to refer to a person?
quests.targetClause: The first person that arrives will get a free ticket.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence correctly uses 'that' to refer to a person?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' can correctly refer to people in defining clauses, and here it is the subject of 'arrives.' 'Whom' cannot be used as a subject, 'which' cannot refer to a person, and dropping the pronoun entirely creates a run-on sentence.
quests.nativeTip: 'That' can refer to people too, but it still needs to play the correct grammatical role and the sentence still needs a relative pronoun.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The first person that arrives will get a free ticket."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Pronoun 'that' for Things
quests.questionSentence: I just deleted an old photo ___ embarrassed me every time I saw it.
quests.completedSentence: I just deleted an old photo that embarrassed me every time I saw it.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' is a natural, correct choice for defining clauses about things such as a photo; it functions here as the subject of 'embarrassed.'
quests.nativeTip: Since 'that' works for things too, check whether the antecedent is a person or an object before ruling it out.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Pronoun 'that' for Things
quests.questionSentence: The umbrella ___ was leaning by the door finally dried out.
quests.completedSentence: The umbrella that was leaning by the door finally dried out.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' is a natural, correct subject pronoun for things in a defining clause; 'who,' 'whom,' and 'whose' all refer to people or possession.
quests.nativeTip: An umbrella is a thing, so rule out any pronoun reserved only for people.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: A dog was barking outside. The dog woke up the whole street. Which sentence correctly combines these ideas?
quests.targetClause: The dog which was barking outside woke up the whole street.
quests.completedSentence: A dog was barking outside. The dog woke up the whole street. Which sentence correctly combines these ideas?
quests.ruleExplanation: Since a dog is an animal, 'which' (or 'that') is correct. 'Who' wrongly humanizes the dog, 'whom' wrongly uses an object pronoun in subject position, and the last option drops the relative pronoun entirely, breaking the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Check three things: is the antecedent a person or an animal, is the pronoun playing the subject or object role, and is a relative pronoun even present?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The dog which was barking outside woke up the whole street."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with who
quests.questionSentence: I finally met the author ___ wrote my favorite childhood book.
quests.completedSentence: I finally met the author who wrote my favorite childhood book.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' is correct because the author, a person, is the subject of 'wrote.'
quests.nativeTip: Find the verb 'wrote' and ask who performed that action.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Antecedent Identification
quests.questionSentence: The manager of the store that closes at midnight called an emergency meeting. What does 'that closes at midnight' describe?
quests.completedSentence: The manager of the store that closes at midnight called an emergency meeting. What does 'that closes at midnight' describe?
quests.ruleExplanation: The verb 'closes' logically belongs to 'the store,' not 'the manager,' even though 'store' is not the very first noun in the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Read the clause itself - what closes? A manager doesn't close, so check what the verb logically belongs to.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Antecedent Identification
quests.questionSentence: My brother's dog that never stops barking kept the whole building awake. What does 'that never stops barking' refer to?
quests.completedSentence: My brother's dog that never stops barking kept the whole building awake. What does 'that never stops barking' refer to?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'My brother's' simply shows possession; the dog is the one barking, so 'dog' is the true antecedent, not 'my brother.'
quests.nativeTip: Possessive phrases like 'my brother's' show ownership, not the antecedent itself - look at the noun that owns the barking.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: The report from the finance team ___ arrived this morning needs urgent review.
quests.completedSentence: The report from the finance team which arrived this morning needs urgent review.
quests.ruleExplanation: The report - not the finance team - is what arrived, and since a report is a thing, 'which' is the correct subject pronoun.
quests.nativeTip: Decide first what actually 'arrived' - was it the finance team or the report itself?

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Clause Recognition
quests.questionSentence: The photo that hangs above the fireplace was taken in 1985. Which words make up the main clause once you remove the relative clause?
quests.completedSentence: The photo that hangs above the fireplace was taken in 1985. Which words make up the main clause once you remove the relative clause?
quests.ruleExplanation: Removing 'that hangs above the fireplace' leaves the complete main clause, 'The photo was taken in 1985,' showing that the relative clause is extra, insertable information.
quests.nativeTip: Try covering up the words that start with 'that' - what sentence is left standing on its own?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The photo was taken in 1985."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: The suitcase ___ was sitting by the gate belonged to a stranger.
quests.completedSentence: The suitcase which was sitting by the gate belonged to a stranger.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' is correct because a suitcase is a thing and is the subject of 'was sitting.'
quests.nativeTip: The gap sits between the antecedent and its verb - decide what 'was sitting' refers to.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with who
quests.questionSentence: The scientist ___ discovered the vaccine later won a Nobel Prize.
quests.completedSentence: The scientist who discovered the vaccine later won a Nobel Prize.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' is correct since the scientist, a person, is the one who 'discovered' the vaccine.
quests.nativeTip: The scientist performs the discovering - check who is acting, not being acted upon.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: The airline ___ cancelled our flight offered no explanation.
quests.completedSentence: The airline which cancelled our flight offered no explanation.
quests.ruleExplanation: Companies and organizations are grammatically treated as things, so 'which' (or 'that') is correct, not 'who.'
quests.nativeTip: An airline is an organization, not an individual person - treat it grammatically like a thing.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: The team ___ won the championship celebrated all night.
quests.completedSentence: The team which won the championship celebrated all night.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' is correct because a team, as a collective noun, is treated grammatically as a thing, unlike an individual person.
quests.nativeTip: Even though a team is made up of people, grammatically the group itself is treated as a single thing.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with who
quests.questionSentence: The coach ___ trained the team for ten years retired last spring.
quests.completedSentence: The coach who trained the team for ten years retired last spring.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' is correct because the coach is an individual person and the subject of 'trained,' unlike the collective 'team' in the earlier examples.
quests.nativeTip: Unlike the team itself, the coach is a specific individual - apply the rule for people.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Antecedent Identification
quests.questionSentence: The instructions inside the box ___ came with the new blender were confusing.
quests.completedSentence: The instructions inside the box which came with the new blender were confusing.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Instructions' - not 'the box' - is what came with the blender, and since instructions are things, 'which' is correct.
quests.nativeTip: 'Inside the box' just tells you where the instructions were - find what actually 'came' with the blender.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Antecedent Identification
quests.questionSentence: The daughter of my neighbor ___ just graduated from medical school moved back home.
quests.completedSentence: The daughter of my neighbor who just graduated from medical school moved back home.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' is correct because 'the daughter' - a person - is the one who graduated, even though 'neighbor' sits closer to the gap.
quests.nativeTip: 'Of my neighbor' explains whose daughter she is - it doesn't change who actually graduated.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
quests.targetClause: The keys which belong to my sister are on the table.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Keys' are things, so 'which' fits, and it correctly functions as the subject of 'belong.' The other options either misassign a personal pronoun to an object or delete the necessary connector entirely.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether the antecedent is a person or a thing, then check whether the pronoun is doing the job of a subject.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The keys which belong to my sister are on the table."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: Our bank ___ handles thousands of customers daily rarely answers the phone.
quests.completedSentence: Our bank which handles thousands of customers daily rarely answers the phone.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' is correct because a bank is an institution, grammatically treated as a thing, and is the subject of 'handles.'
quests.nativeTip: A bank is an institution, like the airline and team you've seen before - treat it as a thing.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Antecedent Identification
quests.questionSentence: The landlord of the apartment ___ finally fixed the heater apologized for the delay.
quests.completedSentence: The landlord of the apartment who finally fixed the heater apologized for the delay.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The landlord' - a person - is who fixed the heater, so 'who' is correct despite 'apartment' sitting closer to the gap.
quests.nativeTip: 'Of the apartment' tells you which landlord we mean - it doesn't change who actually fixed the heater.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Clause with which
quests.questionSentence: A charity is helping flood victims. The charity relies only on donations. Which sentence correctly combines these ideas?
quests.targetClause: The charity which relies only on donations is helping flood victims.
quests.completedSentence: A charity is helping flood victims. The charity relies only on donations. Which sentence correctly combines these ideas?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' correctly refers to the charity (an organization, treated as a thing) and is required to link the two ideas. 'Whom' and 'who' wrongly treat it like a person, and leaving out the pronoun entirely breaks the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Remember: organizations behave like things grammatically, and every relative clause needs its connecting pronoun.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The charity which relies only on donations is helping flood victims."
